response: Growth hormone replacement therapy has been found to have a positive effect on mortality rates in adults with growth hormone deficiency. Specifically, studies have shown that men with growth hormone deficiency who receive growth hormone treatment have a mortality rate similar to that of the background population. In women, after excluding high-risk patients, mortality rates were also similar to the background population, except for cardiovascular disease. Additionally, mortality due to malignancies was not elevated in adults receiving growth hormone treatment. However, it's essential to consider that the heterogeneous etiology of growth hormone deficiency, as well as gender, can influence mortality rates in adults with growth hormone deficiency who receive growth hormone treatment. Overall, growth hormone replacement therapy appears to have a neutral or potentially beneficial effect on mortality in adults with growth hormone deficiency.
